_comment: Where a submitted link belongs, and how it gets filled in.
The source is read off the URL rather than asked for, because the sender
should not have to know that github.com goes to /builds and news.ycombinator.com
goes to /threads. One table, read by three things: the endpoint (to stamp each
row), the /submit page (to show what it detected and pre-pick the topic), and
scripts/submissions.mjs (to route a pulled row into the right queue file).
`column` is the repo queue a source's rows are pulled into — the same files the
ingest-* scripts write, because a submitted link and a discovered link become
the same kind of candidate and are read by the same person. A null column means
there is no home for it: the platform's API is closed to us, or it is just some
blog. Those still queue, and a human still reads them; they simply cannot be
enriched automatically.
`source` values are the ones already in lib/data/jev-*.json (github, x, hn,
devto, youtube). Do not invent a parallel vocabulary — the id prefixes in the
ingest scripts (gh:, x:, hn:, yt:) are derived from these.

`seed` is the URL list an ingest script reads, for sources that cannot be searched. X is the only one today: its ingest takes URLs because there is no affordable read API to query. A source with a seed can be fed by scripts/submissions.mjs seed; the rest need a search query or a hand-written row, and the script says so.
`label` and `enrich` are shown to senders on /submit — the page builds its
"which platforms work" table from this file rather than restating it, so the
answer to "does GitHub work? what about this other site?" cannot drift out of
date. Write them as a table cell: a capital and a full stop.

sources.label: X
sources.enrich: No affordable read API — we open the post and write the quote, media and metrics in by hand.

sources.label: Bluesky
sources.enrich: Bluesky answers 403 to us, so a person opens these.

sources.label: dev.to
sources.enrich: The dev.to API gives reactions and reading time.

sources.label: GitHub
sources.enrich: The GitHub API gives stars, licence and last push.

sources.label: Hacker News
sources.enrich: The Algolia API gives score and comment count.

sources.label: Hugging Face
sources.enrich: A model card or an open release: read by hand, and often a stealth-model lead.

sources.label: Lobsters
sources.enrich: Lobsters answers 400 to us, so a person opens these.

sources.label: Reddit
sources.enrich: Its API is closed to us (403, and app creation is blocked), so a person opens these.

sources.label: YouTube
sources.enrich: The Data API gives title, duration and thumbnail.

fallback.label: Web
fallback.enrich: Any other host — nothing is read for us, so a person opens it.
